reviewType: independent AI sense-aware selected new-owner collision audit
scope: All 22 proposed-new owner rows matching a prior detector at the current 226-selected checkpoint; decisions remain provisional and unpublished

records.sourceExample: Guests should show up before noon.
records.priorMeaning: Be present when needed and offer support, especially in show up for someone.
records.reason: The new source uses show up for arrival before noon. Prior 364 teaches presence as support for a person (show up for their children); same surface verb but different learner choice.

records.sourceExample: Our timing is too tight if we rely on the final train.
records.priorMeaning: Depend on a person, service, resource or method for something needed.
records.reason: Prior 256 only matches the subordinate rely on the final train. Timing is too tight describes an inadequate schedule margin, a separate target and decision.

records.sourceExample: I packed the documents so everything was ready to go.
records.priorMeaning: Very full of people in the stated place or event.
records.reason: Prior 434 matches packed as the literal action of packing documents, while its lesson teaches a crowded venue. Ready to go means prepared for use/departure.

records.sourceExample: Her argument was grounded in facts rather than speculation.
records.priorMeaning: Feeling calm, steady and connected to practical reality or immediate life; more grounded explicitly compares this state with before.
records.reason: Grounded in facts means an argument is evidence-based; prior 798 teaches a person feeling calm and emotionally steady. Shared grounded form has different subject and sense.

records.sourceExample: The opening scene should pull them in at once.
records.priorMeaning: At the same time; this lesson focuses on simultaneous actions or demands.
records.reason: Prior 048 matches the incidental at once adjunct, not pull them in. However canonical 137 draw you in and 428 draw people in already teach attracting an audience with an opening; pull them in changes the verb but appears to repeat the same outcome. Require an explicit lexical-form rationale or merge with an existing attraction lesson.

records.sourceExample: A short reply may come across as rude.
records.priorMeaning: Find or meet someone or something by chance.
records.reason: Come across as rude means create an impression; prior 120 come across means find/encounter by chance. The shorter detector catches a prefix of the longer construction but not its meaning.

records.sourceExample: The film relied on star power to fill cinemas.
records.priorMeaning: Depend on a person, service, resource or method for something needed.
records.reason: Prior 256 detects relied on, the ordinary dependency verb in the sentence. Star power names celebrity appeal that fills cinemas, a separate phrase and learning target.

records.proposedPhrase: keep your feet on the ground
records.sourceExample: It is wise to keep your feet on the ground after a big win.
records.priorMeaning: In the actual local situation where work happens, rather than only in plans or distant descriptions.
records.reason: Keep your feet on the ground after a win means remain realistic/humble. Prior 536 on the ground means in actual local operations; its detector is only a substring of the longer idiom.

records.sourceExample: The schedule ended up running their life.
records.priorMeaning: Eventually reach a result or find yourself doing something, often without originally intending it. The examples here mainly show an initial purpose turning into comparison.
records.reason: Prior 041 detects ended up, an eventual-result frame. Running their life conveys a schedule controlling daily choices, which is a different predicate in the same sentence.

records.sourceExample: The effects will show up in the final results.
records.priorMeaning: Be present when needed and offer support, especially in show up for someone.
records.reason: Effects show up in results means become visible or evident. Prior 364 show up for someone teaches supportive presence; this is a further sense distinct also from 2123 arrival.

records.sourceExample: Teenagers can become caught up in social pressure online.
records.priorMeaning: Talk and share recent news after time apart.
records.reason: Become caught up in social pressure means become entangled/absorbed in pressure; prior 1521 catching up means exchange news after time apart.

records.sourceExample: An unknown artist can blow up overnight online.
records.priorMeaning: Very quickly or almost suddenly, not necessarily during one literal night.
records.reason: Prior 061 overnight contributes rapid timing; blow up overnight additionally teaches sudden growth in an unknown artist’s online fame. The speed adverb is not the proposed target unit.

records.sourceExample: Do not read serious claims with your brain switched off.
records.priorMeaning: Stop thinking about work or worries for a while and relax.
records.reason: Reading with your brain switched off is uncritical/inattentive reading; prior 375 switch off after work means deliberately relax from worries. Subject, purpose and valence differ.

records.sourceExample: Officials have their hands on the wheel during a crisis.
records.priorMeaning: Involving direct practical participation rather than only observing or studying theory.
records.reason: Hands on the wheel during a crisis depicts officials retaining steering/control; prior 329 hands-on means direct practical participation. Prior 925 handing others the steering wheel reverses who gains control, so this new agency frame also differs.

records.sourceExample: The celebration is not worth picking up the pieces afterwards.
records.priorMeaning: Acquire knowledge or a skill informally through exposure or activity rather than only direct teaching.
records.reason: Prior 441 pick up is informal acquisition of knowledge and only matches the prefix of picking up the pieces. The longer idiom suggests recovery after a damaging aftermath, but the isolated celebration sentence does not specify what was damaged or what recovery entails; confirm a teachable, grounded scenario before new-owner approval.

records.sourceExample: She is even-tempered under pressure.
records.priorMeaning: Facing stress, demands or a strong expectation to act.
records.reason: Even-tempered denotes a stable calm disposition; prior 486 under pressure denotes the stressful condition. The latter is a separate modifier in the source, not the target adjective.

records.sourceExample: The plan was falling apart after the second delay.
records.priorMeaning: Become so upset that it is difficult to think calmly or deal with the immediate situation.
records.reason: The plan was falling apart means an inanimate plan is breaking down. Prior 1164 teaches a person too emotionally distressed to cope. Nearby 098 adds at the seams and 521 narrows to practical basics; retain explicit plan-subject boundary and human owner sign-off.

records.sourceExample: Her parents have her best interests at heart.
records.priorMeaning: In someone’s basic nature or deepest interests, even if outward roles suggest something else.
records.reason: Have her best interests at heart is a welfare-motive construction; prior 562 at heart describes underlying personal nature. The detector hits a substring but the frame and learner outcome differ.

records.sourceExample: The device gathered dust once the novelty wears off.
records.priorMeaning: Remain unused or neglected for a period.
records.reason: Prior 1056 gathers dust is a separate unused-device consequence, but canonical 568 the shine soon wears off already teaches initial attraction fading after familiarity. Novelty wears off uses the same predicate and learning outcome with a synonym subject; assess a 568 scope/alias expansion before approving a new owner.

records.sourceExample: Children grow out of clothes remarkably quickly.
records.priorTitle: grow out of real daily life
records.priorMeaning: Develop from an existing experience, need or situation.
records.reason: Grow out of clothes means children become too large for garments. Prior 957 grow out of real daily life means develop from an experience or need; same phrasal verb, different sense and object role.

records.sourceExample: A traditional product need not be stuck in the past.
records.priorMeaning: Remain clearly in someone’s memory.
records.reason: Stuck in the past means constrained by old ways; prior 131 stick in my mind means remain memorable. Stem overlap causes the regex match, not shared sense.

records.sourceExample: A festival changes shape when it enters a new culture.
records.priorMeaning: Influence how something develops or how someone thinks or behaves.
records.reason: A festival changes shape means takes a different form across cultures; prior 020 shape is an active influence verb. Prior 759 take shape means begin to form, another distinct phase.

actionable.2295: Editorial owner comparison with canonical 137/428: require a distinct lexical-usage decision or merge; a detector hit on 048 does not settle this.
actionable.2956: Hold source-quality/teachable-context decision until aftermath and repair can be grounded without invention.
actionable.3703: Compare with canonical 568; likely same fading-novelty lesson outcome and candidate for alias/merge.

limitations: The 22 are detector-overlap leads in selected decision files only, not an exhaustive semantic duplicate search. Classification is independent AI editorial advice, not human owner approval. No decision, lesson, manifest, or release file was changed.
